turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Come on in, Marguerite. Good to see you. It's been about four months since we last went through everything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Four months, yes. Feels like less.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How have things been going with the sugars?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not great, honestly. The morning numbers have been higher than they used to be.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That matches what I'm seeing. Your control has drifted and we're not at goal anymore.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that bad?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It means we do something about it rather than leave it another four months.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I've got today's A1c back — it's eight point four, up from seven point one — and I've read through the letter from the eye clinic in January.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How are you getting on with the metformin?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take it twice a day. And the long acting insulin at night, same as before.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: There is one thing. My feet have been tingling at night. A burning sort of feeling, it keeps me awake.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How long has that been going on?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A few months. It's worse once I'm in bed.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me have a look at your feet. Pedal pulses are present on both sides. Monofilament sensation is reduced across the left forefoot.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So what you're describing, together with the reduced sensation I've just found, is diabetic peripheral neuropathy. It's the diabetes affecting the nerves in the feet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I didn't know it could do that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Your kidney numbers have moved as well. The eGFR is forty four, and there's albumin showing in the urine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What does that mean for me?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It means the kidneys are filtering less well than they were. We'll keep a close eye on it and there's plenty we can do.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm going to increase the metformin to one gram twice daily, and I want to start you on an SGLT2 inhibitor, which helps the sugars and protects the kidneys at the same time.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Alright. Whatever you think is best.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: One more thing before you go. Are you still smoking?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: About ten a day. I keep meaning to stop.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's actually do something about it today. I'd like you to try nicotine replacement, the patches, and I'll refer you through to the stop smoking service this afternoon.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll give it a go.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good. Repeat bloods in three months and I'll see you back then.
